---
title: "Quantifying PTMs in Single-Cell Proteomics"
subtitle: "A reproducible pipeline, end to end"
---

This site is the analysis companion to ***Improved discovery and quantification of
post-translational modifications in single-cell proteomics*** — a re-analysis of
single-cell proteomics data from ALS (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis) motor neurons
([original dataset](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2023.113636)).

It walks through the full workflow, from raw spectra to publication figures, so that
the analysis can be reproduced or adapted to a new dataset.

## The pipeline at a glance

| Step | Tool | Purpose | Output |
|------|------|---------|--------|
| [1](01-metamorpheus.qmd) | **MetaMorpheus** | Peptide/protein identification + PTM discovery (GPTMD) | `AllPSMs.psmtsv`, `AllPeptides.psmtsv` |
| [2](02-flashlfq.qmd) | **FlashLFQ + PIP-ECHO** | Label-free quantification with FDR-controlled match-between-runs | `QuantifiedPeptides.tsv`, `QuantifiedProteins.tsv` |
| [3](03-limpa.qmd) | **limpa** | Dropout-curve modeling, protein summarization, probabilistic imputation | `EList` objects |
| [4](04-r-analysis.qmd) | **R (limma / tidyverse)** | Differential abundance, PTM-occupancy analysis, figures | Figures 1–4 |

## The central question

Most single-cell proteomics studies search with a *limited* set of modifications. We ask
what changes when the same cells are searched against a **diverse** panel of PTMs:

- How many additional peptidoforms and modification types are discovered?
- Do modified peptidoforms carry differential-abundance signal that a limited search misses?
- Where do protein-level conclusions diverge between the two search strategies?

Throughout, two parallel searches are compared:

- **Diverse PTMs** — GPTMD + search against the UniProt human XML, allowing a broad PTM panel.
- **Limited PTMs** — GPTMD + search against the UniProt human FASTA, restricted to three
  variable modifications (deamidation, pyroglutamate, oxidation of methionine).

## The dataset

~100 single motor neurons stratified by TDP-43 pathology severity (CTL / NON / MLD / MOD / SEV),
from five post-mortem donors.

## Reproducing this work

1. **Install the tools** — MetaMorpheus, FlashLFQ, R (≥ 4.3) with `limpa`, `limma`, and `tidyverse`.
2. **Steps 1–3** require the raw `.raw`/`.mzML` spectra, which are not redistributed here. Follow
   the linked pages to regenerate the quantification tables.
3. **Step 4** runs directly from the quantification tables included in the repository under
   `Data/` (large tables are tracked with [Git LFS](https://git-lfs.com)). Open
   `Quantification_of_PTMs.Rproj` in RStudio and source `MainManuscript/analysis.R`, then
   `MainManuscript/plotting.R`.

> The code in these pages is shown for reference and is **not executed when the site is built**,
> because the raw inputs are not public. The figures shown are the actual manuscript outputs.

All source code lives in the
[GitHub repository](https://github.com/Alexander-Sol/Quantification_of_PTMs_2026).
